subject: Consistent finishes across a commercial interior
hook: Signing off a finish for a whole building? The route from sample to installation looks like this.
ig:
Signing off a finish for a whole building? The route from sample to installation looks like this.

Consistency on a commercial job is decided early. By fit day, it's either right or it isn't.

1. View samples in the building itself, under its lighting, next to what's staying.
2. Write a finish schedule: decor, edging and handle for each furniture type.
3. Build the cutting list with decor and grain direction on every panel.
4. Make, edge and assemble in the workshop, comparing doors side by side.
5. Fit each piece in its planned position.
6. Keep the schedule on file for future additions.

Step 1 catches the most problems. Office lighting is often cool and bright, and a board that looked warm in a showroom can look quite different under it.

Save this if you're responsible for a fit-out, and share it with whoever signs off the finishes.
fb:
If you're in charge of choosing finishes for a business premises, this one's for you.

The most useful thing you can do is look at samples in the building itself. Office lighting is usually cooler and brighter than a showroom, and a finish that looked warm elsewhere can change completely. From there, we write up a finish schedule, plan every panel on the cutting list and make it all in our Hanley workshop.

We've set out the full route in this carousel. See finished work from our workshop here:
https://superiofurniture.com/showcase/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=productive-spaces-and-home-offices&utm_content=day-257
